full_judgment:
Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Borguna to show cause as to why the proceedings of criminal Misc. Case No. 474 of 2002 now pending before the court of learned Session judge, Borguna should not be quashed. 

 2. The complaint petition filed by the opposite party No.1 Zahirul Islam (Ex-public prosecutor) Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 475 of 2002 was started against the petitioner on the ground of false education certificate. 

 6. The accused petitioner preferred miscellaneous application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the criminal proceeding of criminal Misc. case No.475 of 2002 pending in the court of learned sessions judge Barguna and obtained instant rule. 

 7. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the educational certificates of the accused petitioner are all genuine, issued by the proper authority and that the complaint petition initiated by the former public prosecutor against the accused petitioner are false, preposterous to be prosecuted. He further submits that the order sheets of criminal Misc. Case No. 475 of 2002 shows clearly that the learned Sessions Judge opposite party No. 2 and the former public.: prosecutor in connivance and in conspiracy with each other initiated the criminal proceeding against the accused petitioner and the proceeding drawn up at the behest of former public prosecutor Zahirul Islam. He further submits that previously complainant Zahirul Islam was the public prosecutor and he was succeeded by the accused petitioner as public prosecutor. The fued started due to, the post of public prosecutor. He further submits that according section 32 of P.O. 46/72 of Bangladesh legal practitioners and Bar Council Order 1972 no court can take any steps against any Advocate for committing any offence of misconduct. The offence of misconduct of any Advocate exclusively triable by the Bar Council. He further submits that under section 193 Cr. P.C. No. court of sessions shall take cognizance of any offence in criminal jurisdiction. He further submits that learned sessions judge committed illegality in examining complainant and taking other steps which shows the malafide intention of the learned Sessions judge with malice, In support of his contention he cited the case of Dr. Nurul Islam Vs. Government of Bangladesh reported in 33 DLR(AD) —201. He further submits that the proceeding is nothing but harassment of the accused petitioner. In support of his contention he referred the case of Md. Khorshed Ali and ors Vs. The state and another reported in 5 BLD(AD) 223, He also cited the case of Shah Alam Vs. the State reported in 28 DLR 448. The case of A. Kader Chowdhury & ors Vs. The state & ors reported in 36 DLR 148, He also cited the case of Haripada Biswas Vs. The state & another reported in 1982 BLD (AD) 13. The case of Eman Ullah Vs. Abdul Kader and another reported in 11 BLT(HCD)2003. 

 9. We have heard the learned Advocate of both the parties at length and perused the miscellaneous application, supplementary affidavits filed by the accused petitioner. In the instant case Rule was issued against the sessions judge, Barguna who was made opposite party No.2. Learned sessions judge Barguna who is now serving as sessions judge, Narayangonj, After service of notice, the said learned sessions judge opposite party No.2 sent a D.O. letter vide Memo No. 113 DJ. N/IH-1/06 dated 6.4.06 before this court and after considering the same this court passed an order directing the opposite party No.2 to appear before this court positively on 8.5.06. On 8.5.06 Mr. K.S. Nabi the learned senior counsel, former Attorney General of the peoples Republic of Bangladesh and former president of the supreme Court Bar Association submits that he has committed a great mistake by writing D.O. Letter to this court and he is being repented, beg mercy and unqualified apology, considering the facts and circumstances of the case we have exonerated the said learned sessions judge for committing such misdeed. 

 10. It appears that the learned sessions judge on receipt of the complaint petition from the former public prosecutor Mr. Md. Zahirul Islam opposite party No. 1 and after taking evidence on oath of the said complainant he has initiated criminal Misc. case No. 475 of 2002 on 1.8.92 and directed the accused petitioner to submit attested copies of the educational certificate since from S.S.C. to LL.B Examination which he is not authorized to do under the provisions of section 32 of Bangladesh legal practitioners and Bar Council order, 1972 (Presidents order 46 of 1972) section 32(2) Bangladesh legal Practitioners and Bar council order contemplates that upon receipt of complaint made to it by any court or by other person against any such advocate has been guilty of misconduct, Bar council shall, if it does not summarily reject the complaint, refer the case for disposal to a Tribunal constituted under Article 33 of the said order and as such we find that the learned session judge acted beyond his jurisdiction. Further more under sections 190, 193 Cr. P.C. no court of sessions shall take cognizance of any offence as a court of original jurisdiction unless accused has been sent to it by the Magistrate duly empowered in behalf. It has been held in the case of Haripada Biswas Vs. The and another reported in 1982 BLD(AD) 13- 2BCR AD 80/81 that sessions judge can call for record of a proceeding pending before a Mag to for the purposes mentioned in section 435 Cr. P.C. but session judge having no power to take cognizance of an offence or cannot initiate a new proceeding. 

 11. In the instant case, though no cognizance was taken by the sessions judge but he has initiated a new proceeding being Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 475 of 2002 which is malafide, illegal and without jurisdiction not sustainable in law. The said contention was also supported in the case of Emanullah Vs. Abdul Kader and another reported in 11 BLT (HCD)6: 

 12. We have gone through the order dated 1.8.02, 3.8.02, 6.8.02, 7.8.02, 10.8.02, 11.8.02, 13.8.02 and 18.8.02 passed by the learned sessions judge which amounts to harassment of the accused petitioner. In the case of Md. Khurshid Ali and others Vs. The state reported in 5 BLD (AD) 223 held that the proceeding would be of no useful purpose and this would amount to unnecessary harassment and as such proceeding is liable to be quashed. In the case of Shah Alam Vs. The state reported in 28.DLR 448 held that wherein allegation in the FIR even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, did not constitute offence as alleged, then no question of appreciating evidence arises, In the case of A. Kader Chowdhury & ors. Vs. The State & ors, reported in 36 DLR-148 held criminal proceeding started on complaint which does, not contain any definite accusation against the accused deems to a abuse of the process of the court and liable to be quashed. 

 13. In the instant case we find that the Bar Council made enquiry with the university and other organization and after enquiry issued a letter to the secretary of Borguna District Bar Association .Borgunavide Memo No. BBC/S.2/2002/2537 dated 7.9.02 stating that: 

 14. The facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above we find that the instant criminal proceeding was initiated at the beliast and malafide intention of the complainant opposite party No. 1Mr. Md. Zahirul Islam regarding the fued of Public prosecutor ship and learned sessions judge acted illegally and aided to the said complainant and intentionally harassed and humiliated the petitioner in the society. The role of the complainant opposite party No.1 is very dirty and dubious. In such circumstances he should not be given the charge of public prosecutor ship in future which is a very important post of judiciary: 

 15. In the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above the rule merits consideration. 

 In the result the rule is made absolute with the above observation. The entire criminal proceeding of criminal Misc. Case No. 475 of 2002 pending in the court of the learned sessions judge Borguna is hereby quashed. The order sheet from 1.2.02 to 18.8.02 passed by the learned sessions judge Borguna in criminal Miscellaneous case No. 475 of 2002 are hereby Set aside. Learned Sessions judge is also directed to hand over the valuable educational certificates and sanad of Advocate ship of the petitioner within 3(three) days from the date of receipt of judgment and order or the certified copy of the same produced before him, which ever is earlier. A copy of the judgment and order be sent to the Ministry of law and parliamentary affairs.
